notes.drag: carriage drag: none until a source gives one
notes.generation: 3: Tor-M1 (weapons.ibx's generation 3 = 1983–1995); keys only its weapons.ibx section
notes.kind: the engine's radar SAM (630) for a radio-command missile: chaff decoys it (inferred)
notes.power: one hit destroys a fighter (inferred, as the AIM-9M)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; held by blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead (docs/real-weapons.md §1.4) times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (15 kg)
notes.range_km: 12 km is marked "citation needed" in the article
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion._spiralAccelBeta: top speed a / beta: 120 / the top speed
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the missile's launch zone from rest (combat.gd fires from the unit's pose at speed 0; missile.rs dlz with "burn": the distance travelled in burn + 4 s) is its published range
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)
notes.motion._fireReleaseInterval: open: the reader's default 0.5 s (combat.gd); one missile in the air at a time (docs/ai.md §14)
